what_happened: The job "Add post-mortem field and retry findings" (20261026-065228-02zf) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 1 of 3 the critic said the plan needed revising and that the reading misread the request. The reading assumed stored verifier findings already have a "resolved" state. They don't: the Finding record (records.rs:750) holds only severity, summary, evidence, location and source. So the "unresolved findings" half of the request had no defined meaning. The critic found two major problems. (1) The plan said the new third Jev question can fail on its own. The real client's parse_response rejects the whole reply when any answer is missing, so the new question could wipe out the class and repeat answers in production. The FakeJev tests would not catch this. (2) The plan added a `resolved` flag that nothing ever sets, so "resolved findings are left out" is shown only on hand-made data. There were three minor findings: reading.rs and tests/introspection.rs are not among the reading's deliverables, and a seeded retry lists all findings while the new section lists only blocker and major ones. The critic confirmed the plan is otherwise well placed. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Nothing checks a reading's assumptions about stored data and real client behavior against the code before the plan is built. The reading took "unresolved findings" to be a field that exists, and took the Jev answers to be read independently. Neither holds in records.rs or jev.rs. The critic is the first stage to open those files, so the gap shows up only in planning, with a three-round cap and no partial plan kept. The reading also left out the files the design touches (reading.rs, tests/introspection.rs), as in the sibling planning failures. A fake client in tests hides the real client's all-or-nothing parsing. Nothing requires a reading to name each data field or behavior it depends on and where it exists today.
prevention: Before a reading is accepted, run a check that every field, state, role or function the reading relies on is found in the current snapshot (by grep of the named symbols). It should flag any dependency that is absent, such as a "resolved" state on Finding, and require the reading to either define it as a deliverable or drop it. For changes to a parsed external reply format, require the reading to list the real parser's failure behavior and a test against the real parser, not only the fake. It should also require every file the design touches to be in the deliverables.
proposed_request: Add a post-mortem field and retry findings to Athena. Outcomes: (1) A retried job's producer brief includes the previous attempt's blocker and major verifier findings (summary, evidence, location), listed the same way in the seeded and unseeded retry paths. There is no "resolved" state on Finding today, so do not invent one. Treat all stored findings from the previous attempt as the ones to carry, and say so in the docs. (2) The introspection record gets a post-mortem field, written by the Jev introspection step. A missing or malformed post-mortem answer must not discard the class and repeat answers: parse_response in crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs must still accept the reply and leave the field empty. Allowed files: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs, the records and introspection code, crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs, docs/decisions.md (new decision), docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md. Acceptance: - A retry brief test shows the previous attempt's findings appear in both the seeded and unseeded cases. - A test using the real Jev parse_response (not FakeJev) shows a reply missing the post-mortem answer still yields class and repeat answers. - A record written with a post-mortem reads back with it. - cargo fmt, clippy and test all pass.
